Dominus Infernus is a limited unique hat that was published in the marketplace by Roblox Roblox is the official account representing Roblox Corporation. Learn more. on July 20, 2010. It could have initially been purchased for 26,000 Robux with 26 copies in stock. It is the second hat in the Dominus series. As of May 4, 2025, 18 copies exist and it has been favorited 129,736 times.

The Torero is one of the limited-time vehicles in Jailbreak. Added on September 3, 2021, it is the fourth vehicle added in the 5 Days of Vehicles Update 2021.

Unlike other vehicles introduced in the update, it was available only for a limited time of nine days and became unobtainable on September 12, 2021.[1] It costed 599,000.

Contents

  • 1 Overview
  • 2 Performance
  • 3 Gallery
  • 4 Trivia
    • 4.1 Miscellaneous Trivia
  • 5 References

Overview

Based off the 1980s Lamborghini Countach, the Torero spawned on a platform placed on the River, located near the Cheater Island. A light beam was placed on the platform so players could find its spawn from anywhere on the map. The platform was removed on the date of the vehicle's retirement.

Performance

Overall, the Torero is a phenomenal limited-time vehicle. Despite being based on a vintage supercar from the 1970s, the Torero has impressive performance that outpaces some of Jailbreak's modern supercars.

The Torero's powerful launch and rapid acceleration complement a high top speed. It has capable brakes and handling, and additionally, the vehicle has a notably fast reverse speed and top-notch off-road capabilities.

Stats
Toggle details
Top speed
Excellent
 Reverse speed
Excellent
The Torero has a top speed of 220 MPH, which is ahead of the Roadster. One of the fastest in-game, being able to reach 88 MPH, it is comparable to the M12 Molten, but slower than the Crown.
Launch
Phenomenal
 Acceleration
Incredible
Reaching 85 MPH in a single second, its launch is one of the best in the game. It's equal to the Polaire, but beaten by Bluebird and Volt. The Torero’s acceleration is incredible. Because of this vehicle having one of the best launches out of any vehicle in the game, it ties for 0-150 MPH acceleration in the game with the Successor and the Power-1. It is only behind the Katana, Polaire, Bluebird and Volt in that aspect. It takes 3.5s to reach 150 MPH and only 6 seconds to hit 180 MPH. However, it slows down a bit after hitting 180 MPH. It's better than Stormrider and only loses to Roadster, Volt, Bluebird, Polaire, Katana and Manta in this stat.
Handling
Excellent
 Off-Roading
Phenomenal
Due to it's relatively small size, the Torero can be controlled with ease at any speed, however, it becomes more difficult to control at higher speeds. Comparable to the Megalodon. Off-roading performance is the best among all supercars, with its amazing traction allowing it to climb mountains and steep hills with ease. It can usually climb hills at a nearly 90-degree angle, a trait sometimes shared with the M12 Molten, Trailblazer and Concept.
Braking
Phenomenal
 Durability
Fair
Its braking is one of the best in-game, stopping within 0.7 seconds from top speed. It is comparable to the Successor. The Torero has the same durability as most Hypercars of 75 HP with a disable duration of 7.5 seconds.

Ram Slowdown Duration/Pit Manuever Cooldown: 2s

Trivia

  • The Torero is SampleModeler's favorite vehicle in-game.
    • He has made this statement four times. The first time in a tweet in 2022[2], the second time in a QNA session in the same year[3], the third time in a tweet in 2023[4], and lastly in a QnA session in 2025[5].
  • The Torero, along with the Concept, are the only vehicles in the 5 Days of Vehicles Update 2021 that are not community-created models.
  • "Torero" means "bullfighter" in multiple Romance languages, so the vehicle's name is most likely referencing the bull on Lamborghini's logo.
  • The popular game series Grand Theft Auto uses Torero as the name for the Lamborghini Countach equivalent as well.
    • The Torero in Grand Theft Auto was released before the Torero in Jailbreak. This suggests that Grand Theft Auto was a likely inspiration for the name.
  • Dogs cannot sit inside of the Torero.
    • SampleModeler had mentioned that there is no space for the dog to fit inside. The dog was to be seated on the windshield, but it would always pop out of the seat.[6]
      • The dog stays outside of the vehicle, similar to the ATV, Patrol, Dirtbike, Frost Crawler and the Volt.
  • The reason why SampleModeler decided to add the Torero to the game was that he was "always obsessed with the 70s/80s wedge shaped cars that aimed for a futurism look."[7]
  • The Torero's in game top speed when stock is the same as the real life counterpart's top speed, that being 182mph.
  • The Torero's license plate used to read 'LIMITED' upon release. However, it was later changed, with the license plate being moved lower and the "LIMITED" plaque added.

Miscellaneous Trivia

  • The Torero has a accompanying garage piece, the Torero Wing.
    • However, unlike other accompanying garage pieces, the wing was added as a Season 23 Level 4 prize, 3 years after the Torero's release.
    • The wing is also positioned a little bit back compared to its real life counterpart.
  • The Torero is the fourth Lamborghini in the game, after La Matador, Surus and M12 Molten.
  • The Torero has the 5th shortest obtainability in the game, only being available for 9 days.
    • The vehicle with the shortest obtainability was the Javelin, which was only available for 2 days, followed by the Parisian, which were available for 4 days, followed by the Agent, which was obtainable for 6 days, and the Aperture, which was obtainable for 7 days (1 week).
